answer: A transitive trust-graph protocol curbs Sybil attacks by bounding peer admission using random-walk bottleneck cuts. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of establishing organic, authenticated peer edges per identity. Without genuine trust relationships, automated clones remain stranded on an identity island, unable to extend a malicious jetty into the core transaction lagoon. A key limitation is that honest new agents suffer high cold-start friction before accumulating verifiable graph trust.
